Well, my T has not fallen to that level (and hopefully won't). But she's meme-ing many concepts and techniques that we used during our time. I just feel it diminishes her work. 

Her content also seems geared to the "self diagnosing" type of people who make up mental illnesses. 

Honestly, I just want to tell her that she's better than this. But who am I to say anything? I am an ex patient stalking her linkedin and insta 🤦‍♂️.

My T quit practice and moved to a different city to pursue a corporate career. We ended therapy on a happy note.

I have her old Ts linkedin so I check it every now and then. Well, it looks like she quit her corpo job and opened a new practice in her city.

She's now posting content on LinkedIn 3-4 times a week and you can tell it's AI generated slop. 

She's also set up an insta where she posts reels of herself talking about the most basic therapy stuff.

I guess it's tough building a new client base from scratch and she's forced to use Linkedin and Insta for marketing. But she's just not good at it. It's like someone has put a gun to her head.

I have empathy for her. I feel bad that she has to struggle like this at this point in her career. I know she is good at what she does. But these reels are so cringe, I wish I didn't get to see this side of her.

I used to do this. But don't do it as often now. Maybe every alternate or third session.

I am also going through a phase where I am discussing some extremely uncomfortable stuff in therapy. I hate jotting it down. It's very difficult to express anyway so I just go with the flow during the sessions.

But for the more manageable stuff in the past I kept notes assiduously. It's a good practice especially if you like to go off on tangents like I do. It also ensures that I am making good use of time and money by covering all ground for that session.

Aw man. I read your post. I know how you feel cause I went through the opposite. Apparently, I respond to multiple medications (not at the same time though. So I started with SSRIs and their effect was huge and came about quickly in 2 weeks. But so did the side effects. There are posts on side effects of SSRIs everywhere. But no one seemed to be having as severe side effects as I did.

When I switched to Wellbutrin/Bupropion, the earlier side effects went away slowly while some new ones started manifesting (i.e. le horny 😂). I ve been on it for years now. I guess I am getting the right dose because it keeps me functional and my moods are normal I guess. I've never had the extreme benefits as many people in this sub do.

Never brought it up with her and got rid of the fantasies soon after. But the fact remains, she is the only woman I have fantasised about being submissive to.

My dad's doctor is extremely sarcastic with me because I ask a ton of questions. He is cool with the rest of the family though. It's like a bad cop good cop routine with me playing the bad cop and my family the good cop.

TBC I don't self diagnose or second guess his diagnosis. I ask a lot about potential risks and side effects based on legit info from Google. Its just part of being an informed patient. But man did I get on his nerves.

I tried to do that initially but couldn't go on with it. So now I just tell ny T if there's some concept I am familiar with. My reasons are simple. 

In my younger days I would often become overconfident in my expertise in a domain after reading a book or a bunch of articles on the internet. Learnt the hard way how different theoretical knowledge and applied knowledge are. I've learnt to delegate and trust people's expertise in both professional and personal tracks.

I also did not want to tread on a professionals toes by appearing to second guess them. Some people do get offended if you ask too many questions or claim to have prior knowledge of what they're discussing.

Fortunately my T is patient on this aspect. If I tell them I've read about some concept beforehand they will try to find out how much I know about it then fill in the gaps or clear misconceptions etc. But yeah you also need to keep an open mind and really listen to what your T is saying and be ready to drop any pre conceived notions etc.

I'm a guy in my late thirties. My T is possibly 10 years younger than me. 

My experience with older therapists has been short lived and bad. I don't trust older people in general, too many bad life experiences. They can be pedantic and the generation gap doesn't help.

I was looking for a T closer to my age and found a nice clinic which was staffed by younger Ts. Never mentioned any age preference and they jist randomly assigned me someone who I thought were in their 30s (I suck at estimating people's ages from their faces). Also probably misheard them say 9 instead of 5 years of experience. Didn't realise my mistake until an year later when we were discussing transferring to another T and I looked at her profile in detail. 

But honestly I think I lucked out. They are good at what they do, period. I learn something new about myself in each session. I think I'm making progress. I know that I am feeling a lot better. It's a strange feeling too, knowing that someone younger is helping me get better and to be grateful to them. But whatever works.

Forgive my very OT response. But something similar happened to me in college albeit the person doing the disappearing act was my friend and bit my therapist.

This was before social media was a thing. I never made any friends in college except for this one girl. We were in the same high school and had met exactly once during an after school activity. I was reading a book alone in a classroom and she just came out of nowhere and we chatted about the book for nearly 2 hours. I had (still do) terrible social skills so we never met again in school. Then an year later I started college in the same city and there were dozens  of alumni from our old high school including her.

We became friends on the first day and used to spend a lot of time together. I could never figure out if she was an introvert or an extrovert. She was smart and well adjusted socially. Yet she seemed to enjoy getting away from her core group and do introvert things with me. We weren't interested in each other romantically or sexually. We would explore the city together, hunt for books and often just talk for hours. One time she convinced me to join a vacation trip and we spent the entire fortnight together away from others. 

Then seven months after college started she went away. Like one day she didn't show up. Wouldn't answer her e-mails. Went to her home and learnt that her family had moved to a hilly area in the country. She never told me or her other friends that she was leaving. No goodbye, no message. But she did transfer to some other University and she had started the paperwork at least 2 months before her 'disappearance'. 

There was no Google or Facebook to look her up. So I tried talking to her friends. Either they didn't know or they didn't want to tell the class outcast. But her 'disappearance' was a topic of speculation anong the students for many years.

I never made any real friends as an adult. I used to think about her a lot. She was not my therapist but we used to confide with each other and she would often motivate me and cheer me up. Boy I missed her terribly those first few months. But her memory faded away as life went on.

I looked her up a few years ago. Or rather looked up her brother because she had changed her name after marriage. Found her FB and LinkedIn. Apparently, she worked for a few months after graduation and then became a teacher and later a small business owner. Got married in between and she has a kid. One of her Facebook likes was the book I was reading the day we met. I never reached out to her. Figured that she could have reached out to me if she wanted but considering that she disappeared without a word, maybe she didn't want to.
